mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-37.3, -26.4, -20.3, -13.4), reflecting self-reinforcing recovery momentum as consumer confidence and foot traffic build on prior gains; this trend should persist, lifting RETAIL_REC further over the next 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC plateaus or declines within the next two weeks absent any new restriction announcement, the momentum-continuation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 8 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, as observed from t-2w to t-0w (+9.8, +8.0), commuting and errand volumes cross a behavioral threshold that converts into additional shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-over-week increase exceeds 8 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -10.1 to -2.1 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks despite TRANSIT sustaining weekly gains above 8 points, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint rise of WORKPLACES (-28.9 to -11.1) and TRANSIT (-29.3 to -2.1) signals restored commuting routines; the interaction of returning office attendance and transit usage amplifies retail footfall beyond either series' individual effect, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved every week in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC growth does not exceed the sum of effects predicted by WORKPLACES and TRANSIT individually, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a restrictions-easing regime, as RESIDENTIAL time declines (13.0 to 5.4) and GROCERY_PHARM visits rise sharply (-4.1 to 19.0), households shift from home-bound stockpiling toward discretionary errands, a behavioral change that should spill over into increased retail-and-recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for three consecutive weeks while GROCERY_PHARM rises
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines while RESIDENTIAL keeps falling and GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising, the behavioral spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp acceleration in GROCERY_PHARM (from -4.1 to +19.0 over three weeks) resembles pre-emptive stockpiling ahead of anticipated tightening of social-distancing policy in response to rising case loads; if restrictions tighten, RETAIL_REC will reverse and decline over the next four weeks despite the recent recovery.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly surge exceeds 10 points while RESIDENTIAL also rises
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose over 23 points in three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next four weeks without any new restriction announcement despite the GROCERY_PHARM surge, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot falls roughly two weeks after Lunar New Year (Feb 1, 2022); the observed RETAIL_REC recovery partly reflects a seasonal post-holiday rebound as businesses reopen and consumer spending normalizes, and this seasonal boost should continue for approximately one more week before tapering off.
candidate_trigger: within 2 weeks after Lunar New Year holiday period
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is roughly two weeks post Lunar New Year 2022
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC growth does not taper or plateau within one week after the post-holiday rebound period, the seasonal explanation is rejected in favor of a structural trend.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossing from negative to sustained positive percent-change (first positive at t-2w, now +19.0) indicates that panic-buying and stockpiling behavior has fully subsided; this behavioral normalization frees discretionary household spending for retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above baseline (positive percent change) for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM turned positive at t-2w and kept rising
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase within one week after GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and rising, the stockpiling-normalization hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Once WORKPLACES mobility crosses above the -15 percent-change threshold (currently -11.1), it signals substantial relaxation of work-from-home mandates, which historically precedes a two-week lagged increase in RETAIL_REC as office workers resume lunch and after-work shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -11.1 at t-0w, above the -15 threshold
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after WORKPLACES sustains above -15, the policy-threshold mechanism is rejected.
